Newborn Care

The first months — feeding, sleep, daily care, and knowing when to call your doctor, plus recovery for you.

Newborn Care Basics: Your First Days at Home

A calm, practical guide to your first days home with a newborn — feeding cues, sleep basics, safe handling, visitors, and learning to trust yourself as a parent.

Read guide

Breastfeeding: A Beginner’s Guide

Getting started with breastfeeding — latch basics, how often newborns feed, common early challenges, signs baby is getting enough, and where to find real support.

Read guide

Formula Feeding: How to Bottle-Feed Safely

A judgment-free guide to formula feeding — choosing a formula with your provider, safe preparation and sterilizing, amounts by age, and paced bottle feeding.

Read guide

Newborn Sleep: What’s Normal in the First Months

What newborn sleep really looks like — total hours, short cycles, day–night confusion, safe sleep rules, gentle routines, and survival tips for exhausted parents.

Read guide

Bathing and Diapering Your Newborn

How to bathe and diaper a newborn with confidence — sponge baths before the cord falls off, bath temperature and safety, diapering step-by-step, and preventing rash.

Read guide

Umbilical Cord Care and Common Newborn Skin Issues

Simple umbilical cord care, signs of infection to watch for, and a reassuring guide to normal newborn skin — peeling, baby acne, cradle cap, and milia.

Read guide

Recognizing Illness in a Newborn: When to Call the Doctor

A calm guide to newborn warning signs — fever, feeding refusal, breathing trouble, jaundice, dehydration, and lethargy — and why calling early is always right.

Read guide

Postpartum Recovery: Caring for Yourself After Birth

What postpartum recovery really involves — healing after vaginal or cesarean birth, bleeding expectations, rest and nutrition, emotional shifts, and your own checkups.

Read guide

Soothing a Crying Baby and Understanding Colic

Why babies cry, calming techniques that actually help, what colic is and is not, how to cope when nothing works, and when crying deserves a call to the doctor.

Read guide

Newborn Development: The First Three Months

How newborns develop from birth to three months — reflexes, senses, tummy time, first social smiles, and easy everyday ways to support your baby’s growth.

Read guide
